transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, doctor, I guess what finally got me to come in is… after I do it, after I’ve eaten like that, I sit there and look around at all the empty containers, wrappers, whatever it is, and I just feel disgusted with myself. Not just embarrassed, but really ashamed, like I don’t even recognize myself for a minute.

I’ve always tried to be a steady man, you know, in control of myself, dependable. That’s how I see myself, or how I’ve wanted to be seen. And then I’m sitting there with all that mess in front of me, thinking, “What the hell did I just do?” It makes me feel like I’m not that person at all. Like I’ve failed at something basic. That feeling afterward is what’s been getting to me the most.
After these episodes of eating, do you ever make yourself vomit, use laxatives, or exercise excessively to try to control your weight or get rid of the calories?

I don’t really know how to answer that cleanly, doctor. I mean… I don’t think I do those things in some planned-out way, if that’s what you mean. I’ve never really thought of myself as someone who has a routine afterward to “undo” it or anything like that.

Afterward, mostly I just feel awful and kind of sit with it. Sometimes I tell myself I should do better the next day, or I get angry at myself, but as far as making myself throw up or taking something specifically for that, or going out and exercising like crazy right after… I don’t think that’s really what happens with me. At least not that I’ve noticed in that kind of direct way.
Can you describe what it feels like just before you start eating during one of these episodes? Do you feel like you can't stop yourself or control how much you end up eating?

Yeah… yeah, that’s probably the part that scares me, if I’m being honest. Just before it starts, there’s this… I don’t know, this pull. Like I may still be thinking clearly enough to know I shouldn’t start, but it’s like the brakes aren’t catching.

I spent years driving, and on the road you learn discipline. You stay alert, you keep to the rules, you don’t just do whatever impulse pops into your head because people can get hurt. I’ve always taken pride in that, being controlled that way. But with this, once I start eating, it feels like that same discipline just shuts off. And I’ll actually be saying to myself, “Magin, put the fork down. That’s enough. Stop now.” I mean, I’m aware of it while it’s happening.

But then my hand goes back again. And again. It’s not like I’m enjoying it in a normal way by that point. It feels more like something has taken over the decision-making part of me. I keep thinking, “Okay, this is the last bite,” and then I’m already reaching for more before I’ve even finished that thought. So yes, it does feel like I can’t control how much it turns into once it gets going.
Do these episodes happen even when you're not feeling emotionally down or stressed, or do they usually happen when you're feeling upset about something?

I’m not completely sure, doctor. I’ve been trying to think about that because I know it probably matters, but it isn’t always clear to me what sets it off.

Sometimes I can look back and say, yes, I was upset, or I’d had a rough day, or I was feeling tense about something and then it happened. But other times… I don’t know. It doesn’t feel like I was sitting there crying or angry or anything obvious. It can be more like I’m just tired, or restless, or I get home and there’s this empty stretch of time, and then somehow I’m eating.

I guess I haven’t kept track well enough to say, “It only happens when I’m stressed,” because I don’t think I can honestly say that. But I also wouldn’t say it has nothing to do with how I’m feeling. It’s muddled. A lot of the time I don’t even realize what mood I was in until after it’s already happened, and then I’m sitting there trying to make sense of it.
When you’re in the middle of one of these episodes, would you say you feel a complete loss of control, like you can’t stop eating or regulate what or how much you’re eating, even if you wanted to?

Yes… I would say that. I don’t like saying “complete,” because part of me is still there, if that makes sense. I’m not blacked out or unaware. I know what I’m doing, and I’ll be telling myself to stop.

But once I start, it’s like the same discipline I used to have on the road just shuts off. I could drive for hours and stay controlled, follow the rules, keep my mind on what I was doing. With the eating, though, it’s like that control doesn’t respond. I’ll literally be thinking, “Magin, put the fork down. That’s enough. Stop now.” And then my hand just goes back for more anyway.

So yes, it feels like I can’t regulate it once it’s moving. I may want to stop, I may even be ashamed while it’s happening, but wanting to stop doesn’t seem to make my body listen. It’s like I’m watching myself keep going past the point where I meant to quit.
How often do these episodes happen, and would you say they’re causing significant distress or affecting your ability to function normally in your daily life?

Since I’ve been home with this back injury, it’s been… honestly, several nights most weeks. Not every single night, but enough that it feels like it’s become part of the week now, which is hard for me to admit.

I keep trying to tell myself, “Well, maybe this week was just a bad week,” but when I look back over the last three months, I can’t think of one week where it didn’t happen at least once. Not one. And a lot of the weeks it’s more than that — several nights, like I said.

As far as distress, yes. It bothers me a lot. It’s not just, “Oh, I ate too much.” It sits with me. I feel ashamed and frustrated afterward, and it makes the days feel heavier because I’m thinking about what happened the night before and worrying it’s going to happen again. It’s affecting me, yeah. I don’t feel like I’m functioning like myself.
